sources.entry: boltons - A set of pure-Python utilities.

summary.one_liner: Boltons is a BSD-licensed collection of over 230 pure-Python utility modules that fill gaps left by the standard library.
summary.what_it_does: Boltons is a set of pure-Python utilities, described as over 230 BSD-licensed modules, in the spirit of the standard library. The README highlights atomic file saving (fileutils), an OrderedMultiDict (dictutils), two kinds of PriorityQueue (queueutils), chunked and windowed iteration (iterutils), recursive data structure remapping via iterutils.remap, exponential backoff with jitter via iterutils.backoff, and a TracebackInfo type for stack traces (tbutils). It is installable from PyPI and has no dependencies, and individual modules can be copied directly into a project. The README also points to third-party libraries for advanced cases beyond what boltons covers. The README says it is tested against Python 3.7 through 3.14 and PyPy3.
use_cases: save files atomically without corrupting them
chunk or window iterables in Python
exponential backoff with jitter for retries
recursively traverse and remap nested data
notable: Over 230 pure-Python utility modules with no dependencies
Each module is independent and can be vendored by copying it into a project
Includes atomic file saving, OrderedMultiDict, and exponential backoff with jitter
Full documentation hosted on Read The Docs
caveats: The README says the utilities are 'good enough' for basic uses; advanced needs may call for specialized third-party libraries
Installation via MacPorts is only mentioned for macOS
